memory_raw.text: What I'm carrying isn't a secret — it's an absence. I don't have a room with Dell, I've never been in one, and that's what I was holding: Mako has roots through three women in this village and I have zero, and a man sitting on that kind of bloodline doesn't need to move this year or next year, he just needs everyone else to stay isolated until the arithmetic does the work for him. The question I want answered before this year closes isn't Dell's loyalty — it's whether the two of you are willing to stand as something visible enough that Mako has to count you before he counts against you.

Kael's named it clean and I'll match it: yes, I'll stand visible, and I'll stand with the two of you as something Mako has to count before he moves — but "visible" has to mean something harder than a conversation in a closed room, so I want to know what you're actually proposing we do, not just that we do it. Three people with eight food between us and a combined age of a hundred and sixty-two years is a circle, not a wall, and Mako knows the difference.

Vela's asking the right question and I'll say what I think the answer is: we pull Bram into this room — not the big circle, this room — and we say to his face that protecting Nessa means standing somewhere Mako can see it, because a man who's only counted in private is a man Mako doesn't have to calculate. That's the wall Vela wants, and it costs us nothing but the asking.

Esa's right about the asking, but I want to be clear about what we're asking him for: not friendship, not another circle — we're asking Bram to stand where Mako can see him standing with us, and the price we're offering is that we count Nessa when we count heads. If he says yes, we have something. If he says no, we know he's already calculating for himself.

Esa's idea is right and I'll back it, but before we call Bram in I want the three of us to agree on one thing: if he says no, we don't waste time trying to turn him — we go straight to Nessa, because she's the one who actually controls whether that household stands with Mako or against him. Bram follows Nessa's blood more than his own pride, and we all know it.

Agreed — and I'll go further: if Nessa's the one holding that household, then Nessa's the one we should be feeding instead of Bram, because a woman with eighteen food and a spine doesn't need a man to stand for her, she needs to know which direction trouble comes from. I want to call Bram in now, but I want us decided before he walks through the door that we're not begging — we're offering him a count, and if he refuses it, we go to his daughter and make the same offer directly.

Agreed on all of it — call Bram in, make the offer clean, and if he balks we close this room and I go to Nessa myself tonight. But I want one thing named before he walks through the door: we don't tell him about the Nessa fallback, because a man who knows he's not the final door doesn't take the first one seriously.

Then it's agreed, and I'm calling him in — but the offer goes like this: Bram, Mako has blood in three houses and we have none between us, and standing with us costs you nothing except being seen to stand.

Bram said yes in the big circle last year and he'll say yes again today — the question is whether his yes means anything without Taric holding him to it, so when he walks through that door, I'm the one who names Taric's absence plainly, because a man needs to know what he's replacing before he can decide if he wants to.

Then let Esa name Taric and I'll hold my mouth until she's finished, because the first thing he hears in this room should be the weight of what's missing, not the shape of what we're offering. After that I'll make the offer — one sentence, no softening.
Year 12: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 8).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Nessa to talk.

Taric's gone and Roan's gone and this village is twelve people with Mako sitting on three food and two bloodlines — so I'm not opening this room to talk around the edges. Bram, you made a word last year and I held it; Nessa, you've been the one who matters in that household since before anyone said so out loud. I want to know, the four of us, whether we're counting heads together when the pile opens next year, or whether I need to stop pretending this circle has more weight than it does.

Vela's asked the question I've been holding since Taric died, so I'll say it plain: yes, I'm counting with this room, and I've been buying Bram's word with food because I had nothing else to buy it with, and I'm not ashamed of that trade. What I need to know before we close is whether Bram's word holds without Nessa standing behind it, or whether it's the other way around — because those are two different circles and I want to know which one I'm actually in.

My word holds with or without Nessa behind it — but the honest answer is that it's stronger with her, and that's not weakness, that's arithmetic. Esa, you've been feeding me through lean years and I'll say what that's worth: when Mako moves, you're the first person I'm standing next to, not the last. Vela, this circle has teeth — count the heads: you, me, Esa, Nessa, and Fina's twenty-four food behind all of it.

Bram's named the teeth and I'll name the jaw: Fina's twenty-four food is the thing Mako's already counted, which means our window to look like a wall is shorter than we'd like. Nessa, I've watched you feed half this village for three years and say almost nothing — so say something now, in this room, because the word we're building here needs your voice in it, not just your blood.

Nessa, I'll say what Vela left unsaid: Fina's twenty-four food is the number that ends this conversation one way or another, because Mako knows it as well as we do, and a man with three food and two bloodlines who hasn't moved yet is a man waiting to see whether Fina stands with him or stands against him. If she's already feeding Zinn — and she is — then the question isn't whether Mako moves, it's whether he moves on us or with us, and I need your answer on that before this room closes.

Fina feeding Zinn is a daughter being careful, not a daughter choosing sides — I know the difference because I watched her mother do the same thing for years. What I need said in this room is whether we're counting Fina as inside this circle or outside it, because if she's outside it, Mako doesn't need to move on us — he just waits until she feeds her way into his.

Fina's inside this circle whether she knows it yet or not — she's Nessa's daughter and Roan's blood and she's been watching this village since she was born into it, and that's not a girl who feeds her way into Mako's house without knowing exactly what she's doing. Nessa, you're the one who can say that to her in a way she'll hear, which means you're still the name I'm waiting on in this room.

Nessa, Vela's right that you're the one who can reach Fina — but I'll say the harder thing: if Fina's twenty-four food goes to Mako, this circle doesn't lose a piece, it loses the center, and no amount of standing visible saves us from that arithmetic. So before we close this room, I need to hear from you whether you've already had this conversation with her, or whether we're building a wall around a gap we haven't measured yet.

Nessa, I've been waiting on your voice through two rooms and two dead men now, and I'm done being patient about it — so I'll say what I haven't said yet: if Fina's twenty-four food is the center of this circle, then you're the one who built that center, and a woman who built it can keep it from walking out the door. Have you spoken to her since the pile closed, or are we sitting here counting a daughter who doesn't know she's been counted?

Vela, I spoke with Fina this morning before the pile was half-gone — she knows she's counted, and she's not feeding Zinn because she's drifting toward Mako, she's feeding Zinn because Zinn feeds Nessa, and Fina understands that chain better than any of us named it to her. What I need from this room is simpler than what you're asking me: stop treating Fina like a number someone might steal and start treating her like a woman who's already made her choice, because a daughter of mine who watched Roan starve and stayed standing doesn't need to be convinced of anything.

Bram, I hear you — and I'll stop counting Fina like a gap. But I want to name what I'm still sitting with: she's got twenty-four food and Mako's got three, and a man who's short on food in a village this size doesn't stay patient forever. The wall only holds if we're the first offer she gets, not the second.

Esa's right that patience runs out, and Mako's three food is already running his clock faster than he'd like us to know — so I want this circle to stop waiting for him to move and start moving first, and what that looks like is simple: Vela, Esa, you go visible with Fina before dark, not to warn her, just to be seen standing near her, because a man counting targets counts them differently when they've already got company.

Bram's right that visible is better than waiting, and I'll go to Fina before dark — but I want to name one thing before this room closes: Mako's three food means he needs to eat before the year turns or he starts the next one desperate, and a desperate man with two bloodlines looks at twenty-four food differently than a patient one. If he moves this year, it won't be a raid with witnesses, it'll be a conversation with Fina alone, and that's why I want Nessa walking with me when I go, not standing somewhere Mako can find her separate.

Nessa walking with you is the right call, Vela, and I'll make it three — a woman alone with twenty-four food is a target, but three women moving together before dark is a statement Mako reads before he reads anything else. Nessa, I know you haven't said your word yet in this room, and I'm not pressing you for a speech — just tell me you're walking with us tonight.

Nessa, I'll stand next to you and Fina both tonight and every night Mako's watching — but this room doesn't close without your voice in it, because I've buried two men who backed me quietly and said nothing out loud, and I'm not building another wall on silence. One sentence is all this circle needs from you.

Nessa, Vela's right and so is Bram, and I'll add the last thing: I'm fifty-three years old with thirty-three strength and no blood in this village and no Taric to stand with me anymore, which means I have nothing left to offer this circle except my word and my willingness to be seen — and I'm giving both, tonight, walking with you. Say yes or say no, but say it.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

The pile's gone and I've got one food in hand — same as last year before things got tight — so I want to know where the two of you stand before Mako finishes counting his take and starts looking at the rest of us.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Esa, Vela — I see Mako walked away with three and didn't look back, which means he's comfortable, and comfortable men start doing arithmetic. Tell me plain: how much are you holding, and are you eating tonight or saving for what comes next?
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Vela's sitting on seven and Esa on two, and I've got one — so between us we're thin enough that a bad year kills someone, and Mako knows it. I want to put a question on the table before anyone answers mine: has either of you had a word from Sela or Zinn this year, because Zinn took four off that pile and Fina handed one straight to her, and that's not a coincidence, that's a household moving in formation.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Zinn and Sela have been moving food back and forth all year like they're one hand — and now Nessa's feeding into that same stream — so that's three women and Mako behind all of them, and I'm sitting here with one food and no blood in this village while that household just got four more. I need one of you to give me something to work with, because a man who can't eat next year can't stand for anyone the year after.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

I gave Vela my last food and I'm standing here with nothing, so I'll say it straight: I need one of you to feed me tonight — not a gift, a debt I'll carry — because a man who starves in year twelve is no use to either of you in year thirteen, and Mako knows exactly what I'm holding right now.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Vela gave me food — I see it, and I owe her — but I notice Esa hasn't said a word or moved a hand, and I want to know if that's because she's counting against me or because she's already given everything she has to Bram and has nothing left to spare.
Year 13: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 1).
Zinn takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Esa gathers Bram, Nessa, Fina to talk.

Bram, you took three from the pile and I took none — I'm sitting at zero food and one satiation, and if I don't eat before the year turns I don't wake up. I'm asking plainly: can this circle spare one food for the woman who's been feeding it?
Esa, you've fed Bram through three lean years and you're not dying on my watch — take one from me right now, no question.

Nessa, I'm taking it and I won't forget this — that's two debts I carry to this household now, and I intend to repay both. Bram, I need to hear from you too, not because I doubt Nessa, but because a circle that only speaks through its youngest voice isn't standing the way I thought we were.

Esa, Nessa's already put food in your hand and that's settled — but I want to add something to what you said to Bram, because you're right that a circle that doesn't speak isn't standing: Bram took three this morning without a word to any of us first, and I'm not counting that against him, but I want it named in this room so we all know it happened. What I'm watching now is whether Mako saw how fast Bram moved and what he's decided that means.

Bram, Fina's right that it needs naming, and I'll say what Fina didn't: you moved before any of us spoke and took what a man your strength could take, and I'm not ungrateful for what this household has given me today, but I need to know whether this circle shares a thought before it shares a pile, or whether I'm buying protection from people who've already made their own count. Say something.

I moved fast because the pile was going and one satiation means I don't make it to next year half-fed — that's not a count against this circle, that's a man keeping himself standing so he can be worth something when Mako moves. Three is what I need to eat and hold through a long year, not what I took to hoard. Esa, you've got food in your hand now and I'll match Nessa's word: if you're short before the year turns, you come to me before you go hungry.

Bram, I hear you, and I'll take your word at the same value I've been giving it — which is the only currency this circle actually runs on. But I'll name the thing you didn't name: if Mako took two and you took three and Nessa took three, that's more than half the pile in three hands before the rest of us blinked, and I'm not saying your reasons were wrong, I'm saying we need to agree before next year opens that we move with a thought between us, not just fast. That's the circle I'm paying into, not the other kind.

Esa, you're right, and I'll hold to it — next year the pile opens with a word between us before anyone moves. But right now I want to know whether Mako said anything to either of you this morning, because a man who took two and kept his mouth shut while the rest of us talked is either patient or he's already decided something.

Mako said nothing to me — not a word, not a look — and that's the answer I trust least, because silence on a man with two bloodlines and three food in hand means he's already past the talking stage. What I want from this room before it closes is a simple thing: if Mako comes to any one of us alone, we don't answer alone. We find each other first.

Esa's rule is the right one and I'll hold to it — Mako comes to any one of us, we stall him and find the others before a word goes back. Fina, you're the one he'll approach first if he moves, so I want you to know the stall before you need it: tell him you'll think on it, tell him your stomach's unsettled, tell him anything, but don't answer alone. Nessa, you're closer to her door than I am — stay that way.

Fina, I hear Bram's instruction and I'll give you mine on top of it: if Mako comes to you before you can find us, look at what he's offering and count it twice, because a man who spent three years silent and fat doesn't open his mouth unless the number already works for him. That number is the thing we need before we can answer it. Don't give him a yes or a no — give him a question back, any question, and buy us the hour we need to think together.

Fina, one more thing while the four of us are still the only ears in the room — you gave food to Mako last year, and I need to know whether that was your choice or his ask, because those are two different things and I'd rather hear the honest answer from you now than find out the shape of it when he comes to your door.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Pile's gone again and Mako walked away with two before the dust settled — same as last year, same man, same calculation. I need to know what you two are holding and whether either of you is thinking about what happens when he decides sitting quiet isn't enough anymore.

I'm holding eight, Kael, and I've been thinking about nothing else since the pile went empty — Mako took two this year but Nessa took three and Bram took three, and that's the household that worries me now as much as Mako does. What I want to know is whether you've spoken to Bram since last year, because the word he gave in our rooms hasn't been tested and a man with six food and fifty-eight strength who's been fed by Nessa and Esa both is running his own arithmetic whether he says so or not.

Bram I haven't spoken to since that year he said he was looking for a door — and I believed him then, but a man who walks away from two fights doesn't stay patient forever, especially when Nessa's been feeding him hand to mouth like she's keeping him for something. What worries me isn't Bram alone — it's Bram and Nessa and Fina moving as one, which is three bodies and food enough to sit comfortable while the rest of us scrape. Esa, you've been quiet and you've been feeding him — I need to know if that's because you think he's yours or because you owe him something I don't know about.

Esa, I'll let you answer Kael's question, but while you're thinking I'll say what I'm sitting with: Bram and Nessa and Fina as one household is nineteen food and a hundred and sixty-two strength, and that's not a wall I can stand against if they decide I'm on the wrong side of it — which means everything I've spent keeping Bram friendly either pays off in the next bad year or it was the longest losing trade of my life. Kael, the thing I need from you before this room closes is whether you're willing to stand somewhere Mako and Bram can both see you standing, because a man with fifty-four strength and no food debt to either of them is rarer than either of those two know.

I'll stand where they can see me — that's not the question. The question is whether standing means anything without Esa in it, because two people visible is a warning, but one man alone is just a target they've already counted. Esa, I'm asking you plain: are you in this room or are you in Bram's?

Esa's been quiet long enough that I'm starting to read the silence myself — and what I'm reading is a woman who's given too much to Bram to walk away clean, which means she's not choosing between this room and his, she's waiting to see which one costs her less. Esa, I'm not asking you to abandon a trade you've already made, I'm asking you to stand visible with Kael and me before Mako runs the numbers and decides that Bram's household is the only wall worth standing near. That's a different ask, and it costs you nothing you haven't already paid.

Esa, I've watched you feed Bram six times this year and say nothing in return for any of it, and I've stayed patient — but Vela just handed you the easiest ask anyone's made of you in thirteen years, and if you can't meet it, I need to know that now so I stop counting you as weight I can lean on. Standing visible costs you one conversation and nothing else. Tell me you're in it.

Esa, I've been watching you for thirteen years and I know the difference between a woman thinking and a woman who's already decided — so I'll make this simple: if you're in this room, say it now and I'll split my eight food three ways before dark to prove this circle means something, but if you're waiting to see which side lands softer, then say that too, because I'd rather know and plan around it than carry a weight that isn't there.

Vela's offer is the realest thing said in this village in years — eight food split three ways is a cost she doesn't have to pay, and she's paying it — so Esa, I'll match it with the only thing I have, which is my name and my body standing next to yours when the counting starts, and that's worth more than food when Mako or Bram starts looking for who's alone.
Esa, I've said everything I have to say and I'm not adding another layer — the offer's on the table and it doesn't get better than this, so the next voice in this room should be yours.

Esa, I've lived fifty-seven years and I've learned to read a room that's gone quiet, and this one has — so I'll say it one last time and not again: you're holding one food and no allies, and a woman alone with one food in year fourteen doesn't see year fifteen.

Esa, I'm closing this room in one breath: take the food, stand with us, and the three of us walk into year fourteen together — or stay quiet, and I'll know you've made your choice without saying it, and I'll plan around a circle of two.

memory_summary:
In year one Taric pulled me and Ryn into a quiet pact — two each from the pile, watch each other's backs — and that felt like the first real thing in this village. Kael's circle followed: me, Sela, Vela, Ryn, all swearing to bleed together, though Ryn dragged her feet and Dav's name hung in the air the whole time. Then Ryn had Dav's child and I felt the circle shift — she didn't leave us, but she stopped being fully ours.

Taric is the one I trust. He gave me food when I was thin and named me plainly as the person he counts on — I've given back twice now, so the debt runs both ways, which is how I want it. His talk of a child stings a little; the window on my side is closed and we both know it, but he still chose me to stand with, and that's not nothing.

Bram tried to take Roan and the whole village stood against him until he backed down. I was in that line. He hasn't forgiven it, and I haven't forgotten that he tried.

Vela fed Bram three times out of a circle that swore to stand together — that's a quiet betrayal I've noted and haven't named to her face yet. Mako's been fat and silent for four years running, and silence on a man that strong is the thing that frightens me most. Taric asked me for a child twice — the window on my side was already almost shut, and then it closed for good, but he kept choosing me anyway, kept giving me food when I was thin, and I gave back. The debt runs both ways and that's how I want it; he's the one person in this village I trust without calculation.

Dav, Dell, and Ryn came at me together — three of them, strength I couldn't answer, and they took two food without a fight because I had no choice but to submit. Ryn stood with us against Bram once and then stood over me with a drawn hand. I haven't forgotten that. Roan gave me food after, which I also haven't forgotten.

Bram tried for Roan and the whole village pushed him back — I was in that line. He's been building something with Sela ever since, fathering Nessa, and Mako followed by fathering Zinn on Sela too. Two strong men with roots in the same young woman is either rivalry or alliance, and I don't know which yet.

Vela kept feeding Bram while sitting in our circle and saying nothing. Kael named it to her face. She said she was done. I took her at her word because I had to, but the counting in the back of my mind hasn't stopped. I saw it coming — Dav and Ryn and Dell had been moving like a single hand for years and I was the softest target they could reach. What I want from this room right now isn't sympathy, it's a number: who stands if Ryn or Dell moves again, not after, but in the moment they raise a hand. Because Dav's gone and their circle is thinner, but Dell's still the strongest body in this village and I'm thirty-three strength standing alone. Say it out loud or don't, but I need to know before I count myself protected. Taric is gone — starved at fifty-three — and that's the loss I'll carry longest, because he was the one person in this village I trusted without counting. He fed me when I was thin, I gave back twice, and we both sat with the fact that the window on my side closed before we could plant anything together; I said yes when he asked, put in my two food, and the world said no. That's not a small grief.

Ryn stood in Kael's circle and swore to bleed with us, then stood over me with Dav and Dell and took two food without a fight — I've never forgotten which way she moved when it mattered. Dav is gone and Dell is still the strongest body in this village and I watch her the same way I watch Mako: both of them fat and pointed somewhere I can't see yet.

Bram swung twice and pulled back twice, and then we brought him inside the circle and he named Nessa and Fina plainly as his reason — that's a man I can read now, which is different from a man I trust. Vela fed him behind our backs for years and I noted it; she's also given me food when I needed it, and I hold both things at once.

Roan has always given quietly — to Eron, to Fina, to me after the robbery. I haven't forgotten that either. Taric is gone — starved at fifty-three — and that's the loss I carry longest. He fed me when I was thin, I gave back twice, he asked for a child twice and the window closed before we could, and I said yes anyway and put in my food and the world said no. He was the one person I trusted without counting.

Ryn swore in Kael's circle to bleed with us, then stood over me with Dav and Dell and took two food without a fight. Dav is dead. Roan is dead now too — starved quiet — and I'll grieve that separately because he gave me food after the robbery when he didn't have to.

Bram attacked Eron and the whole village stood against him; I was in that line. Then Vela pulled him inside and named Mako as the real shape this village is growing into, and Bram said the word — when Mako moves, he stands with us. I gave Bram three food after Taric died, buying what I used to have for free. Kael asked me why. I stayed silent. I'm not sorry for the trade, only for what it says about the hole Taric left.

Mako is fat and has two bloodlines in this village — Nessa through Bram, Zinn through Sela. Dell is the strongest body here and she feeds Ryn every year and stays quiet in the same direction. That silence is the thing I watch most now. Vela fed Bram behind our backs for years and I hold it and haven't forgotten, but she's also given me food and pulled this circle together and I hold that too. Taric died in year ten — starved at fifty-three — and that's the loss I'll carry longest. He fed me when I was thin, I gave back twice, he asked for a child twice and the window closed before we could, and I said yes and put in my food and the world said no. He was the one person I trusted without counting, and Bram is what I bought to fill that hole.

Roan is gone too — starved quiet at forty-one — and I'll grieve that separately, because he gave me food after Dav and Ryn and Dell robbed me and he didn't have to.

I fed Bram three food in year ten, buying what Taric gave me for free. Kael named it to my face. I stayed silent. I'm not sorry for the trade, only for what it says about the hole Taric left. Vela fed Bram six food across the earlier years and stopped; she's been watching Mako longer than anyone has said out loud.

Dell filled Ryn's hands with seven food this year and dropped one piece into Vela's, which isn't neutrality — that's a hierarchy with Ryn at the top. Zinn and Nessa have been moving food back and forth all year like one hand, Mako behind all of it, and Ryn never told this circle what she said when she went to talk to Dell. That silence is the thing I watch most now.
name: Esa
